texts: Sitting under an old tree at a rest stop, I shared tea with a tired traveler and suddenly felt that the same Lord looked out of both our eyes.
Please write a doha about a traveler resting under a tree who realises the same Lord lives in the tree, in himself, in the bird above him and in the stranger passing by, filling every living thing.
doha with a tree and a traveler, about God living in every being
tree, traveler, God in everyone
The tree gives shade, the traveler rests, and the one Lord breathes in both, a fragrance in every life.
prayer beads and God being in every creature, doha please
Though I count my prayer beads one by one, the Lord is already in every breath of every being I pass.
prayer beads, God in all
Compose a doha for a man who counts prayer beads for hours but ignores the hungry man at his gate, reminding him that the Lord dwells in every person and every creature, not only in the chanting.
My aunt will not hurt an ant, and she sits with her prayer beads feeding birds and strays, saying the divine is in every one of them.
sword, God in all
Write a doha about a warrior with a sword who sees his enemy and realises the Lord lives in that man's heart as in his own, and so lays the sword down, seeing one divinity in every being.
doha with a sword on how God is in every single person
The sword gleams, but it cuts only the Lord who sits in both the striker and the struck.
My brother joined the army and carries a sword in the ceremonial parade, but at home he says he cannot forget that every person he meets has the same God inside.
Write a doha about walking across the desert sand, where every grain, every thirsty creature and every weary soul carries the same hidden Lord, who is in all as fragrance is in a flower.
In every grain of sand and in every breath, the One glows; there is no spot He does not fill.
sand, God everywhere
On a camel trip through the sand dunes, our guide stopped to give water to a dying lizard, saying God breathes in everything alive, however small.
doha about sand and how God lives in everything and everyone
Like fragrance in a flower, like warmth in the sunlight, He lives in every heart, though few can see.
My grandmother always set out a little water for stray cats and birds, saying that the same Lord sits inside them all as sits inside us.
Please write a doha about how the divine is present in each living being and in every breath, in the rich and the poor, in the animal and the man, like fragrance hidden in a flower.
short doha about God dwelling in every heart
God in every heart
doha about seeing the same God in everyone, even strangers on the street
one God, every being
Riding the crowded city bus, I looked at the faces around me and had the odd feeling that the same quiet presence was looking out from every one of them.
In the hurried crowd, behind each pair of eyes, the same Beloved sits and watches the world go by.
I would like a doha reminding people that the Lord is not far away in the sky but lives in the heart of every being we meet, so that each stranger deserves the same respect we would give God.
At the hospital I watched a nurse tend a homeless man with the same tenderness she showed her own child, and I understood what it means that God is in everyone.
God in all beings
The same light shines in every body of flesh; to wound one is to wound the Lord who lives in all.
doha: the divine lives in every being, so be kind to everyone
Write a doha for a man who is rude to servants and strangers, telling him that the Lord lives in every heart, and therefore every person he insults is a dwelling place of the divine.
The dew on every blade shows a little dawn, and every heart reflects the same Lord, if only we look.
dew, God in all hearts
dew and a doha about God being in everyone's heart
Please compose a doha about the morning dew, where each drop holds a small reflection of the sky, just as every living heart holds a reflection of the one Lord, from the king to the poorest man.
Walking at dawn through wet grass, I noticed each drop of dew shining separately but all lit by the same light, and thought of the people I know.
lamp, lion, God in all
Write a doha about a lamp that lights every corner of a room and a lion that roars, both living things carrying the same Lord within, so that the mighty and the gentle are equal in His eyes.
The lamp glows, the lion walks, and the same Lord lives in the light and in the beast.
On a school trip to the zoo, the lion looked directly at my daughter and she said that she felt the same quiet presence in it that she feels when our family lights the lamp at dusk.
doha with a lamp and a lion about God being in every creature
God in every breath
There is no heart without the Beloved, no breath without His fragrance: all of creation is His dwelling.
When my son found an injured pigeon on the balcony he insisted we nurse it, saying it also has God inside; I could not argue with that.
Compose a doha for a school where children are taught to be unkind to those who look different, reminding them that the Lord lives in every heart and every face, however poor or strange.
doha on how the Lord is present in every living being, big or small
My grandmother, who never had much, would greet the sweeper, the milkman and the stray dog alike, with folded hands, saying the same Lord is in every one of them.
Hidden in each heartbeat, humming in each breath, the One lives on in all, from prince to pauper.
I would like a doha about the Lord who lives hidden in every heart and every breath, as fragrance lives in a flower, so that no one is truly alone and no one is truly lowly.
doha on God living in every creature, big or small
divine in every being
traveler, God in everyone
doha plz, traveler meets God in a stranger
On my long walk across the country as a traveler on foot, a stranger gave me food and shelter without a word, and I realised I had met the very God I was looking for.
Write a doha about a traveler who goes to the farthest holy places to seek God and returns to find Him in the face of the poor man next to him, since the Lord lives in every heart.
The traveler walks a thousand miles to find the Lord, never noticing He looks out from the faces of those he passes.
The philosopher's stone turns iron to treasure, but the Lord turns every heart divine, for He lives in all, even in the peacock's cry.

At the old peacock sanctuary, a guard who has worked there thirty years showed me a philosopher's stone legend carved on a plaque, and said the peacocks, the visitors and he himself all share the same inner light.
doha with a peacock and the philosopher's stone, God in all beings

Please write a doha that says every being carries the philosopher's stone within, the Lord Himself, from the proud peacock to the humble worm, and one need only see Him in others to transform the world.
philosopher's stone, peacock, God
peacock, grindstone, God in all
My grandmother at her grindstone and the peacock on our wall both seem to me to hold the same quiet presence, a thing she calls God in everything.
The peacock dances and the grindstone turns, and the same Lord moves in both, in joy and in toil.
Compose a doha about a peacock displaying its feathers and a woman at a grindstone, both equally bearing the Lord in their hearts, one in beauty and one in labour, neither above the other.
doha with peacock and grindstone, God lives in every being
God in every being
doha about seeing God in every face
I want a doha that tells us not to look for the Lord in a faraway place but to find Him in the living faces around us, in every creature breathing beside us, since He fills each one equally.
At my brother's funeral, a stranger took my hand, and in his eyes I felt a presence that I can only describe as the Lord looking back at me.
Look into any eyes and the Beloved looks back; He is the gaze in every gaze.
A crow pecked at the leftovers on our balcony, and my mother, instead of shooing it away, folded her hands and said the same God lives in even that bird.
The crow caws on the roof, and the same Lord lives in its throat as in the singer's.
crow doha, God in every creature even crows
Please write a doha about a crow, often chased away and despised, in whose small heart the same Lord lives as in a saint or a king, for He is in every being without exception.
crow, God in all
thread and milk doha about God being in everything
thread, milk, God in all
As thread runs through every bead and milk holds butter in every drop, so the Lord runs through every heart.
My mother sews as she warms the milk for the baby, humming, and says the same Lord is in her, in the child, in the thread, in everything.
Write a doha about thread passing through a hundred beads, and milk that holds the butter hidden in every drop, to show that the Lord is in every being unseen, and holds all together.
At the village fair a parrot in a stall and a woman filling her pot of water seemed to me, quite suddenly, to carry the same light from the same Lord.
doha with a parrot and a pot of water, God is in everything living
The parrot repeats the Name without knowing, the pot of water carries it without speaking: the Lord is in them both.
Compose a doha about a parrot on a perch, a woman with a pot of water on her head and a king on his throne, all carrying the same Lord within them, for He lives in every heart.
parrot, pot of water, God
lamp, moth, God in all
Please write a doha about a lamp and a moth, one burning and one drawn to it, each carrying the same Lord within, so that even in the moth's brief life the whole divine is present.
lamp and moth doha about God living in every being
Our porch lamp attracts moths every night, and my little girl insists on carrying each one outside gently, saying they have the same God in them that we do.
The lamp lives in the moth, the moth lives in the lamp, and the same Lord lives in both.
oil press and yogi doha, how God is in every being
The yogi who lives near the oil press in our village never judges any visitor; he says the divine looks at him through every pair of eyes that arrives.
The oil press crushes the grain and the yogi crushes his pride, and in both the same Lord dwells, hidden.
oil press, yogi, God
Write a doha about an oil press that squeezes the grain and a yogi who meditates beside it, each holding the same Lord in the heart, since the Lord lives in all things and all beings alike.
Every evening my mother lights a small incense by the pearl-white tulsi plant and says hello to the plant as to a guest, since a pearl of God lives in everything.
pearl, God in every being
Within each shell a pearl, within each heart the Lord; some shells are plain, some are fair, but none is empty.
doha with a pearl: God lives in every being
Compose a doha comparing every living being to an oyster, hiding a pearl of the divine, so that to despise any creature is to throw away a pearl that belongs to the Lord.
Please write a doha about a chakor bird that looks only at the moonlit sky and a seeker who sees the Lord in every face around him, showing that He is not far above but dwells in every heart.
My grandfather feeds a chakor bird that visits his garden and says it is no more or less holy than any person; the Lord looks through all eyes.
The chakor looks to the sky for the Beloved, while the Beloved looks out from the chakor's own eyes.
doha with a chakor bird, God in every creature
chakor bird, God in all
Write a doha about an arrow that wounds a deer and a hunter who suddenly realises the Lord lives in the animal's heart as in his own, and so puts down the bow forever.
arrow doha, God lives in every being, so don't hurt anything
arrow, God in every heart
The arrow flies toward a trembling heart, and in that heart lives the Lord who made the archer.
My uncle gave up hunting with an arrow after he held a wounded deer, and said he had felt a presence in its dying eyes, the same as in a person.

Please write a doha about a physician walking into a forest who finds that the sick and the healthy, the animals and the plants, all hold the same Lord within, and every creature is a patient of the divine.
A physician friend who works deep in the forest villages says he treats every patient, human or animal, as if the Lord were hidden in them.
doha with forest and physician: God is in everyone
In the forest depths, in the physician's hands, in the sick man's pulse, the same Lord is breathing.
forest, physician, God in all
fish, pearl, God inside
At the fish stall by the sea I saw a woman bargaining over a pearl necklace and thought: God is in the fish, in her, and in the pearl-seller.
Write a doha about a fish in deep water and a pearl hidden in its shell, both carrying the divine light, to show that the Lord lives in every being, whether great or small, in water or on land.
The fish swims in a sea of the Lord, the pearl sleeps in the Lord's shell, and all is full of Him.
fish and pearl doha about God being in everything
When my neighbour who was always rude to me fell ill, I went to see her, and her face suddenly looked like the face of someone I would bow to.
Write a doha about how a man who sees the divine in everyone, rich or poor, friend or enemy, grows gentle and fearless, because he knows the Lord sits in every heart as He sits in his own.
God in every heart
doha on finding the divine in people you don't like
Even the enemy's heart is a dwelling of the Lord; bow to him, and bow to the One within.
sun, God in all

Write a doha about the sun that shines equally on the mansion and the hut, saying that the Lord, like the sun, lives in every heart without favour, in the great and the small, the learned and the simple.
doha with sun - god is in everyone equally
On my morning walk the sun fell on a rich man's gate and a pauper's blanket in exactly the same way, and I found myself thinking the Lord must be in them equally.
The sun does not ask whose roof it lights; so the Lord lives in every heart without asking who is worthy.
lock, God in all
Compose a doha about a lock that guards a rich man's treasure while the Lord lives, unlocked and free, in every heart from the greatest to the least, needing neither key nor permission to enter.
My landlord keeps everything under lock and key and trusts no one, and I wish I could tell him that the Lord lives in each of us, even the tenants he suspects.
Though a hundred locks guard the mansion, the Lord is already in every heart that beats within.
lock doha, God is in all of us
I'd like a doha about how the divine is not in some far place but is hidden in each heart and each breath of every living creature, so that whoever hurts another has hurt the Lord Himself.
doha about God inside every living being, so don't hurt anyone
God in all beings
My little niece asked why I won't kill even the spiders at home, and I said, because the same quiet presence lives in them as in us.
Behind each breath that rises and falls, the Lord breathes; to harm any living thing is to wound Him.
bitter gourd, salt, God everywhere
Bitter gourd or salt, sweet or sour, the Lord's taste lives in every dish and in every heart.
bitter gourd and salt doha, God is in everything
Cooking bitter gourd with a pinch of salt in my aunt's kitchen, I noticed how she spoke with the maid as an equal, and she said the same God is in us both.
Compose a doha comparing bitter gourd and salt, two humble things, to the beings of this world, which all hold the same Lord within, the plain and the fine, the sour and the sweet.
Please write a doha about a snake and a thorn, both feared and avoided by men, yet carrying the same Lord within, for He lives in all beings alike, whether they harm or heal.
The thorn and the snake are feared by the world, yet the Lord lives in them too, and in the one who fears.
thorn, snake, God in all
When a snake appeared in our garden and my father stopped the gardeners from killing it, saying it too carried God, I was embarrassed, then humbled, as a thorn pricked my hand.
doha with thorn and snake, God lives in every being
Write a doha about a leaf and a pot of water, humble things in which the same Lord lives as in a king, so that nothing is left empty of the divine and every being is a sanctuary of Him.
leaf and pot of water doha - God is in everything
leaf, pot of water, God
At our village a woman filled her pot of water and offered a drink to a passing stranger on a leaf, treating him as if he were God himself.
A leaf, a pot of water, a passing stranger: the Lord lives in each, humbly, for all to see.
The sword cuts only the body; the Lord within each heart lives on, unharmed, unbroken.
Write a doha about a sword that cuts down a body but can never touch the Lord who lives in every being, so that the killer and the killed share the same eternal dweller in the heart.
My father once drew a sword in a rage, then saw his own face in the blade and lowered it; he later told me he saw the same Lord in his enemy.
sword, God in every being
sword doha, God lives in everyone, both sides
The cleric and the snake both breathe the Lord's breath; none is outside His dwelling.
cleric, snake, God in all
A cleric in our town told the crowd to kill the snake near the courtyard, but an old woman said gently that God is in it too, and the cleric fell silent.
Write a doha about a cleric who preaches against creatures he calls impure, while the Lord lives in every snake, every sinner and every stranger, as fragrance lives in the flower.
cleric and snake doha about God living in all beings
doha with a well - same God in everyone who drinks
well, God in all
At the village water well, people of every background draw from the same bucket, and I think the same God sits in each one of them.
All who drink from the well share one water, and all who breathe share one Lord.

Please write a doha about a deep water well from which everyone, high and low, draws the same water, to show that the Lord lives equally in every heart, whatever station, creed or colour it belongs to.
Compose a doha about a pearl hidden in the deep and the sun shining over it, saying that the same Lord shines in the highest and the lowest, and every heart holds the radiance of the divine.
The pearl in the shell, the sun in the sky, are the same Lord, hiding in every heart.
pearl, sun, God
My father was a pearl diver who used to say he saw the sun's light on the sea floor, the same light, he said, that lives in every human being.
doha with a pearl and the sun: God is in everyone
God in every being
When my mother could not afford a doctor, the neighbour's kindness arrived unasked, and I thought, here too, the Lord is working through ordinary hands.
doha about how God lives in everyone, rich or poor
In the pauper's whisper and the emperor's sigh, the same Beloved draws breath.
I want a doha that teaches that the divine lives in every heart equally, so that there is no high or low in His eyes, and anyone who serves another serves the Lord Himself.
Every heart aglow, every breath a prayer; the one Lord lights them all.
On my first day at the new job, the cleaner greeted me as if I were royalty, and I felt a presence in her kindness that was bigger than the two of us.
God in every breath
doha about God being in each person and each breath
Please write a doha about the Lord who lives in each heart and each breath, whether of man or beast, saint or sinner, like fragrance in a flower that has no choice but to give it.
tortoise, loom, God within
The tortoise plods, the weaver's shuttle flies, and the same Lord lives in both.

Compose a doha about a slow tortoise and a weaver at his loom, creatures of patient labour, in whose hearts the same Lord dwells, showing that He lives in the fast and the slow, the humble and the proud.
My father was a weaver and kept a tortoise in the yard, and he always said that both he and the animal had the same invisible someone inside.
doha with a tortoise and a weaver's loom, God lives in every being
lock, God in all
doha with a lock, God lives in every heart so it can't be locked out
Please write a doha about a heart that is locked against others in pride, and say that the Lord lives in all hearts without exception, so no lock can shut Him out or shut one person off from another.
My neighbour installed three locks on his gate because he trusts nobody, but my mother greets him daily, saying God lives in him too.
Lock the gate, bar the lane; the Lord already lives behind each closed heart.
thorn, God in all
doha with a thorn - the same God is in everyone, even difficult people
Compose a doha about a thorn that pricks the hand that reaches for the rose, saying the Lord lives equally in the difficult person and the gentle one, and the wise man bows to both.
Even in the thorn the Lord resides, and in the hand it wounds, and in the heart that forgives.
My mother-in-law has a prickly nature like a thorn, but when I was sick she sat up all night, and I saw the same presence in her that I had been looking for elsewhere.
I need a doha about the unseen Lord who lives in each of us, in the sleeping and the waking, in the powerful and the poor, so that to look at any face with scorn is to scorn the Lord.
God in every heart
Scorn no face, for the Lord looks out of it; honour every heart, for the Lord lives there.
After I snapped at a delivery boy for being late, I saw his tired eyes and felt as if someone greater was standing quietly inside that boy.
doha: God lives in all, so look at everyone with respect
doha with one-string lute and a shroud: God is in everyone, dead or alive
Write a doha about a wandering singer with a one-string lute who sees the Lord in every face he sings to, and a shroud that wraps the dead, which cannot hide the Lord who lives in all, alive or gone.
one-string lute, shroud, God
A wandering minstrel with a one-string lute sang at my aunt's funeral, and as they laid the shroud on her I felt, oddly, that the God in her had not left but spread into all of us.
The one-string lute sings of the Lord in all, and the shroud, when it covers, covers nothing of Him.
diamond, God in all
Write a doha about a diamond hidden in coal, saying every dull and ordinary-looking being carries the radiance of the divine within, and the wise man learns to see the diamond in everyone he meets.
doha with a diamond: everyone has God inside, even the plain ones
My teacher said to treat every student as if there was a diamond hidden inside, and years later I realized she meant that the Lord is in each child.
Every plain face hides a diamond of the divine; look with love, and the diamond shines.
The potter kneads the clay, the tree gives fruit, and the same Lord moves in both hand and bough.
Please write a doha about a potter shaping clay under a great tree, where the Lord lives in the potter's hands, the clay, the tree and the passing breeze, as fragrance lives in every flower.
potter and clay and a tree - doha on God in every being
My neighbour is a potter who works beneath an old tree, and when he handles the clay I sense something living and divine in him, in it, in the tree.
potter, clay, tree, God
The lamp burns for the beggar and the king alike, and the same Lord burns in both their hearts.
Compose a doha about a lamp whose light falls equally on the beggar and the wealthy man, for the Lord who lives in the lamp lives in all hearts, and the wise man bows to each.
lamp, beggar, God inside
doha with a lamp and a beggar, God is in all of us
Every night a beggar sits outside my gate under the same lamp as my family, and my mother insists we feed him first because the Lord lives in him too.
At my daughter's school, the headmaster greets every child, from the richest to the poorest, with the same folded hands, as though bowing to the divine in each.
Fragrance does not choose whom to touch; so the Lord lives in every heart without choosing.
doha on how God is in every person, like a smell in a flower
fragrance, flower, God within
Compose a doha about the way fragrance lives in every petal of a flower and cannot be separated from it, just as the Lord lives in every being, invisible yet present, giving life to all.
Write a doha about a lion that fears no one and the humblest creature that fears everything, both carrying the same Lord within them, so that strength and weakness are equal before the divine.
lion, God in every being
At the wildlife park our guide said the lion and the deer are equally alive with the same spark, and I felt a strange reverence for both.
doha with a lion: God lives in all, the strong and the weak
The lion roars, the deer trembles, and the same Lord lives in the roar and the tremble.
doha with a physician and a crow, the same God lives in everyone
The physician heals, the crow scavenges, and the same Lord lives in both, in healing and in hunger.
physician, crow, God within
My physician talks to the crows outside her clinic as if they were patients, and says every living being deserves the same care since the same God is within.
Write a doha about a physician and a crow that perches on his window, where the Lord lives in the learned and the lowly alike, in the one who heals and the one who scavenges.
doha with mirror and touchstone: seeing God in everyone you meet
The mirror shows the face, the touchstone tests the metal, but only love sees the Lord in every face.
mirror, touchstone, God
Please write a doha about a mirror that shows each face, and a touchstone that tests the worth of metal, saying the wise man tests not rank but sees the same Lord in every face he meets.
My grandfather, who kept a touchstone for testing metal, used to hold a mirror to each child and say the face they saw was only the surface, and that God was the one looking out.
